why: The answer says the local variable c gets the default value 0. In Java, a local variable has no value until it is assigned, so reading c in c + 1 is a compile error ('variable c might not have been initialized').

concepts.quote: int c; declares c, so c is 0.
concepts.why: This matches the wrong rule that local variables get a default value. Here the code would not compile because c is read before it is assigned.
